topic: The Riemann Zeta Function: Bridging Primes and Analysis

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Infinite Geometric Series
lecture_lines: The infinite geometric series sums to one over one-minus-r.
Euler's formula links products over primes to sums.
Imagine a sieve filtering composite numbers away.
animations: Create a geometric series 1 + r + r^2 +... using white color #FFFFFF.
Highlight terms and show they approach 1/(1-r) when |r|<1 using light blue #ADD8E6.
Display formula 1/(1-r) centrally with bold gold #FFD700 emphasis.

sections.title: Defining the Riemann Zeta Function
lecture_lines: The zeta function sums one over n to power s.
When s is one, this harmonic series diverges infinitely.
If s exceeds one, the series converges nicely.
animations: Display Zeta function sum n^-s for Re(s)>1 in white #FFFFFF.
Highlight the domain Re(s)>1 with light orange #FFCC00 shadow.

sections.title: Analytic Continuation: Mapping the Invisible
lecture_lines: Standard summation only works when s is large.
We use analytic continuation to map the plane.
Think of extending a road beyond the horizon.
animations: Visualize function surface expanding beyond the initial domain in cyan #00FFFF, emerging from a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/horizon.svg].
Show smooth path connecting regions using a glowing trail effect #FFFFFF following a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/road.svg].
Highlight the connection point with a purple #800080 pulsing circle.

sections.title: The Critical Strip and the Hypothesis
lecture_lines: The critical strip lies between zero and one.
Riemann proposed all zeros lie on line half.
Zeros act like nodes on a guitar string.
animations: Draw the critical strip Re(s)=1/2 in light gray #D3D3D3 [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/guitar.svg].
Animate points on the critical line moving upwards in red #FF0000.
Highlight the line Re(s)=1/2 with a bold white #FFFFFF outline [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/guitar.svg].

sections.title: Why It Matters: The Music of the Primes
lecture_lines: Zeros dictate the distribution of prime numbers.
Proving the hypothesis reveals prime number structure.
We predict primes like seeds in a garden.
